findings.title: toEqual comparisons against flat Prisma.sql literals fail because the service composes nested Sql
findings.body: Prisma.sql does not flatten nested templates: when the service composes conditions with `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})`` (the reduces in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions), the inner Sql objects are stored as elements of the outer Sql's `values`, producing strings like `['(', ') OR (', ')']` with Sql instances in `values`. The new assertions build the expectation as one flat template literal (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(("teamId" = ${id}) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (...)``), whose `strings`/`values` structure is completely different (flat strings, scalar values). `toEqual` performs structural deep equality, so these assertions fail even though both would serialize to identical SQL when executed. Affected assertions: team scope (line 295), org scope (line 332), and combined filters (line 429) — the suite this PR delivers will not pass (consistent with the PR description noting the tests were never successfully run). Fix by asserting on executed query results (as the getBaseConditions test does), building the expected Sql with the same composition, or comparing a flattened serialization instead of the raw Sql object.

findings.title: Public findMany() removed without updating any consumers
findings.body: The PR deletes `findMany(findManyArgs)`, previously the only data-access method on InsightsBookingService, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw Prisma.Sql fragment that callers must embed into their own `$queryRaw` against the "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" table. Only the service and its test file are changed in this PR, so any existing caller of `service.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights tRPC/router code) will fail to compile, and consumers now each need to hand-write the raw query. Verify that all consumers are migrated — either in this PR or a clearly stacked one — before merging.

findings.title: getBaseConditions contains unreachable branches with a fail-open shape
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed and implemented to always return a non-null Prisma.Sql (it returns NOTHING_CONDITION `1=0` at worst), so in getBaseConditions the `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }` and final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches are dead code, and the `authConditions &&` check is always truthy. Beyond being dead code, the structure implies a fail-open path: if authorization conditions were ever able to be null (mirroring getFilterConditions' `Prisma.Sql | null` type), the method would return the filter conditions alone and silently drop the authorization predicate. Simplify the method to always AND the never-null auth conditions with the optional filter conditions so it cannot fail open.

findings.title: Order-sensitive ANY array assertions rely on unordered DB queries
findings.body: The org-scope assertion expects the Sql values arrays in an exact order — teamIds `[orgId, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` (line 333) and userIds `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` (line 338) — but TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds issue findMany queries with no ORDER BY, so Postgres row order is not guaranteed (e.g. after autovacuum or with different plans on a busy CI database). Deep equality on the embedded arrays is order-sensitive, making this test flaky. Sort the ids deterministically in the service, or assert on unordered sets / executed query results instead.

findings.title: Caching tests removed while the service still implements caching
findings.body: The PR deletes the entire "Caching" describe block ("should cache authorization conditions" / "should cache filter conditions"), which was the only coverage verifying that repeated calls to getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() reuse the cached result instead of rebuilding (including re-querying memberships). The service still implements this behavior via cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions, so the conversion silently drops coverage of existing behavior. Re-add equivalent assertions using the new Sql format (e.g. asserting a build* method is only invoked once).

findings.title: PR description/diagram claims the service was already converted and is unedited
findings.body: The description's summary states the tests are updated to work with "the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation", and the mermaid diagram marks `insightsBooking.ts` as "Context/No Edit" — but this diff is what converts the service to Prisma.sql and removes its public `findMany` method. This misrepresents the scope of the change to reviewers (the raw-SQL authorization logic is the risky part and is presented as untouched context). Update the summary and diagram so the service conversion is reviewed explicitly.
